newsitem.title: USA: U.S Midcon products prices ease with slack demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S Midcon products prices ease with slack demand.

text.p: U.S. midcontinent refined petroleum products prices eased Monday evening, as sagging demand, especially in distillates, erased early gains inspired by the energy futures markets, traders said.
Refined products generally eased 0.25 cent a gallon in late trade as volume turned light and few deals were struck, traders said.
"You had a stable market...All the buying was for New York (Harbor)," one trader said.
Low sulphur diesel in the Group was offered 0.25 lower than midday at 6.00 cents over May NYMEX.
Soggy conditions in the midwestern U.S. dampened agricultural demand, and cut the bullish tone set earlier Monday as May heating oil worked its way toward a 0.80-cent-a-gallon-rise.
Diesel numbers in Chicago also weakened 0.25 cents, with sellers asking for three cents over the screen and bidders setting their price at 2.75 cents above NYMEX.

Unleaded gasoline in the Group lost ground late, with differentials on the sell side down 45 cents to 70 cents under May NYMEX unleaded gasoline, as demand remains sluggish ahead of the summertime "driving season."
"We've got plenty of gasoline to meet demand growth now and for summer driving season," the trader said.
